title: Monetary Policy and Interest Rates
text: Monetary policy refers to the actions taken by a central bank to influence the money supply and interest rates in order to achieve macroeconomic objectives such as controlling inflation, maximizing employment, and maintaining financial stability. Expansionary monetary policy (lowering interest rates, quantitative easing) stimulates economic activity, while contractionary policy (raising rates) cools an overheating economy. The transmission mechanism describes how monetary policy changes affect the broader economy through credit markets, asset prices, exchange rates, and expectations. Unconventional monetary policy tools, such as negative interest rates and forward guidance, were deployed by major central banks after the 2008 financial crisis.
